methodological_rigor.justification: The study demonstrates exceptional methodological rigor through a large-scale multicenter design (n=115,973 retrospective; n=9,266 prospective) and a robust 39-month ground truth that incorporates interval and next-round cancers. Statistical analysis is highly appropriate, utilizing the Obuchowski variance estimate to account for clustered reader data and applying Holm–Bonferroni corrections for multiple comparisons. The authors explicitly report a power calculation (80% power at site level) and address real-world distribution shifts in the prospective phase through adaptive operating point recalibration.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is classified as LoE 2b as it combines a large-scale retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with a prospective observational feasibility deployment. It demonstrates high clinical relevance by showing that AI can increase cancer detection rates by up to 20% while reducing human reader time by 32%, directly addressing the global radiologist workforce shortage. The inclusion of interval cancer follow-up and prospective technical monitoring provides a robust translational path for integrating AI into national screening programs.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript adheres to the STARD standard for diagnostic accuracy, providing comprehensive details on participant flow, pre-specified noninferiority margins, and prospective/retrospective study designs. It includes clinical trial registration numbers (ISRCTN) and references detailed supplementary protocols and a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary. Data availability is limited to statistical source data for figures, while the raw imaging data and proprietary AI code remain restricted, which is typical for this field but limits full independent replication.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript provides a meaningful extension of prior work by validating an updated AI system (version 1.2) across a large, multicenter NHS cohort and introducing a methodological focus on adaptive operating point calibration to address distribution shifts during prospective deployment. While the core findings regarding AI diagnostic non-inferiority are incremental relative to established prospective trials like MASAI (Lång et al., 2023) and the authors' own previous evaluation (McKinney et al., 2020), the emphasis on implementation science and real-world drift monitoring fills a documented gap in the literature. The positioning is appropriate, correctly identifying that while accuracy is well-studied, the practicalities of technical integration and threshold maintenance remain significant hurdles for clinical adoption.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is exceptionally well-organized and clear, utilizing descriptive subheadings in the results section that effectively guide the reader through complex multicenter data. The abstract is exemplary, providing precise quantitative outcomes for both retrospective and prospective phases, while the discussion offers a sophisticated synthesis of clinical implications and implementation barriers. Figure captions are highly informative and provide necessary statistical context, ensuring the findings are standalone-interpretable.

key_strengths: Large-scale multicenter retrospective validation (n=115,973) with robust 39-month follow-up
Rigorous inclusion of interval and next-round cancers in the ground truth definition
Prospective feasibility deployment addressing real-world distribution shift and threshold calibration
Demonstrated 32% reduction in reader time with a concurrent 17.7-20.2% increase in cancer detection
High-quality reporting following STARD guidelines with detailed statistical methodology
key_concerns: Proprietary nature of the AI system and restricted access to raw imaging data
Relatively short duration of the prospective feasibility phase (8 weeks)
Observed distribution shift between historical and prospective data requiring manual intervention
Limited sample sizes for specific ethnic subgroups in the fairness analysis
chief_reviewer.rationale: This study represents a high-impact validation of AI in a national screening context. Its scale, methodological rigor, and focus on implementation challenges like data drift make it suitable for top-tier clinical or translational journals.
